title: The sower again (Mark 4:1–9)
hookLine: teaching from a boat, he tells of seed thrown everywhere

cards: The crowd on the shore of the Sea of Galilee is so big that Jesus climbs into a boat, pushes out a little, and sits down to teach from the water, with everyone lined up along the beach.

A new part of Mark begins here: chapters four to six, seeds, storms and loaves. And the first thing he says is a single word: listen. Then comes a story you heard on day twenty-three, in Matthew's telling.

teach.b: In the King James Bible it starts: "Hearken; Behold, there went out a sower to sow." Hearken means listen, really listen. The farmer walks his field throwing seed by the handful, and it lands everywhere.
Some on the hard path, and the birds eat it. Some on rocky ground with a thin skin of soil, where it springs up fast, then scorches and withers in the sun. Some among thorns, which choke it.
And some on good ground, where it grows and yields thirty, sixty, a hundred times over. To us the farmer looks careless. Why throw good seed on a path?
Some readers suggest he sowed first and plowed the seed under afterward, which would make broad scattering sensible. Either way, this sower doesn't pick and choose.

teach.h: SEED ON EVERY KIND OF GROUND.
teach.b: Some Christians hear grace in that: the word is offered to every kind of ground, hard, shallow, crowded and ready.
Then Mark closes the story the way he opened it: "He that hath ears to hear, let him hear."

teach.h: HE THAT HATH EARS TO HEAR.
teach.b: The first word was hearken; the last line is about ears. Everything between is a story about how things are received. Tomorrow the disciples admit they didn't get it, and he explains.
For today, notice the parable is wrapped in listening, front and back.

how: Christians read the sower both on its own and with the explanation Jesus gives a few verses later, and sermons on it often ask what kind of ground a life is today.

o: to go back to an earlier time
to listen closely and take it in
to speak up loudly to a crowd

games.q: where the seed landed — tap the pairs.

s: Jesus taught this parable from a boat
the crowd was so big he sat in a boat on the water and taught them on the shore.
the sower carefully chose only the best soil
in the story the seed lands everywhere: path, rocks, thorns and good ground.
the parable begins and ends with listening
it opens with hearken and closes with he that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

games.q: you're the sower. the path is hard, there are rocks and thorns, and only part of the field is good soil. what do you do?
games.why: the seed goes everywhere, and some of it lands on good ground and yields thirty, sixty and a hundredfold.

practice: Listen outward first: name the farthest sound you can hear, then the nearest, traffic, a fridge, birds, your own breathing.
Then listen inward for the quiet thought underneath the busy ones today, and don't answer it; just hear it all the way through, like a seed landing. If you pray, you can offer that listening to God.

wordCard.voice: Hearken, the first word of the sower's story, meaning listen, really listen: the parable is wrapped in it, front and back.

orig.note: Greek: to sow, to scatter. Mark 4:3 uses it twice: a sower went out to sow.

carryVoice: Your line: let anyone with ears hear. The seed went on every kind of ground. See you tomorrow.
